documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28F here to establish. Was seeing a PCP group closer to her old apartment; wants somewhere she can actually reach by text. No complaints today.

PMH: none. Never had a chronic diagnosis.
PSH: tonsils out as a kid (age 8).
Meds: combined OCP — norgestimate/EE 0.25/0.035, one daily, on it for years without issues. No supplements.
Allergies: none to meds.
FH: mom — breast cancer at 55, treated, doing well. Dad — type 2 diabetes.
SH: works as a marketing coordinator, mostly desk and some events. Never smoked. 2-3 drinks a week, social. No drug use. Exercises a few times a week (runs, yoga).
Gyn: periods regular and light on the pill. Last Pap last year at old office, told normal — records requested.
ROS: negative across the board. No headaches, no leg swelling, no chest pain.

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT unremarkable, tonsils surgically absent. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rashes or concerning moles. Extremities without edema. Mood and affect normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. Health maintenance, healthy adult — BP normal on the pill, fine to continue estrogen-containing OCP (nonsmoker, no migraine with aura, no clot history). Refills through us going forward.
2. FH breast cancer in mother at 55 — plan screening mammography starting at 40; no earlier imaging indicated by this history alone. Will revisit if more family history surfaces.
3. FH T2DM — glucose with routine labs next year.
4. Records request to old office for Pap and vaccine history.
Flu and COVID shots when available this fall. RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted Sunday asking to be seen about some bumps; in today.
S: Noticed small skin-colored bumps around the anus starting around early November, maybe 2 months now, a few more than at first. Not painful, no bleeding, no itch to speak of, no change in bowel habits. Mostly bothered by how they look and wants them gone. One partner, together about a year, monogamous. Never had an STI. No prior genital lesions.
Meds: OCP. NKDA.

O: Afebrile, vitals fine. External perianal exam (chaperoned): several flesh-colored, raised papules with a rough, verrucous surface clustered around the anal verge; nontender, no ulceration, no bleeding. No inguinal adenopathy. Vulva grossly without similar lesions.

A/P
Perianal papules, appearance most suggestive of anogenital warts.
- Referral to dermatology for confirmation and treatment; asked them to see her within a few weeks.
- STI screen since these can travel together: HIV, RPR, urine GC/CT. She is fine with this.
- Reviewed that this is common, typically from HPV, and usually treatable. Avoid shaving/picking the area.
Will message results.

documents.title: Your test results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Beth, all the screening from Tuesday is negative — HIV, syphilis, chlamydia and gonorrhea. Dermatology should be calling you to schedule; let me know if you haven't heard by the end of next week.

documents.title: Re: Your test results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Phew, thank you. They called yesterday, I'm in on Feb 10.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP — CONSULTATION
Date of service: 02/10/2025
Referred by: primary care, for perianal papules

Thank you for sending this 30-year-old woman. For roughly three months she has noticed a cluster of growths around the anus. They are skin-toned and do not hurt or bleed. Her main concern is cosmetic; she feels embarrassed by them.

Past medical history: none significant. Surgery: tonsillectomy in childhood (age 8).
Current medications: combined oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate), one tablet daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with breast cancer at 55; father with type 2 diabetes.
Social: in an exclusive relationship for about a year. Denies any previous sexually transmitted infection. Your recent HIV, RPR and GC/CT testing noted as negative.

Examination: Perianal skin shows several verrucous papules measuring 1 to 2 cm encircling the anus. No inguinal or femoral lymphadenopathy. Remainder of the skin and general examination is unremarkable.

Procedure: After informed consent and local anesthesia with 1% lidocaine with epinephrine, a tangential (shave) biopsy of one representative lesion was obtained and sent to pathology. Hemostasis with aluminum chloride. Wound care reviewed.

Impression: Perianal verrucous papules, clinically consistent with condylomata acuminata; histology pending.

Plan: We will call her with pathology. If confirmed, plan for in-office cryotherapy in about 4 weeks, likely requiring more than one session. Partner does not need treatment unless he has visible lesions.

Dermatology

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, perianal, tangential biopsy.
Gross: a tan, papillomatous shave of skin, submitted entirely.
Microscopic: exophytic squamous epithelium with papillomatosis, acanthosis and parakeratosis. Numerous koilocytes are present in the upper epidermis, with perinuclear clearing and wrinkled, hyperchromatic nuclei. No dysplasia is identified. No evidence of malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Skin, perianal, biopsy: condyloma acuminatum (koilocytic change present). Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

documents.title: Pathology report received

documents.title: Biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Beth — I saw the biopsy report from dermatology. It confirms these are genital warts (condyloma), the HPV changes in the skin cells are exactly what we'd expect, and there is nothing precancerous. Dermatology plans freezing treatments starting next month. Your Pap and HPV test in August were normal, so nothing else to do on the cervical side. Happy to talk anytime.

documents.title: Re: Biopsy result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thank you. They already booked me for March 10. Is there anything my boyfriend should do?

documents.title: Re: Biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Only if he notices any bumps himself — then he should see his own doctor. No routine testing for him otherwise.

documents.title: Dermatology Procedure Note
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP — PROCEDURE NOTE
Date of service: 03/10/2025

Pathology confirmed condyloma acuminatum. Biopsy site healed. Lesions unchanged since February.
Medications: combined OCP. Allergies: NKDA.

Procedure: liquid nitrogen cryotherapy to the perianal condylomata, two freeze-thaw cycles per lesion. Tolerated well. Post-procedure blistering and soreness reviewed; sitz baths as needed.

Plan: return in 4 weeks for reassessment and repeat treatment of any residual lesions.

Dermatology

documents.title: Sore after freezing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Had the freezing done Monday. It's pretty sore and a couple spots blistered. No fever. Is that normal or should I call derm?

documents.title: Re: Sore after freezing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's the expected reaction — blisters and soreness for several days are how the treatment works. Warm sitz baths, loose cotton underwear, and ibuprofen or Tylenol if needed. If it gets red and spreading, very painful, drains pus or you get a fever, call dermatology or me the same day.

documents.title: Re: Sore after freezing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok good, thank you!

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN PRACTICE — NEW CONSULTATION
Date of service: 02/16/2026
Reason for referral: new external genital growth

HPI: 31-year-old who comes in with a growth by the external genitalia. She had perianal condylomata in February 2025, treated by dermatology with cryotherapy and cleared. She first saw the new lesion a few weeks ago and thinks it has been slowly enlarging. No pain, discharge or pruritus.

PMH: perianal condylomata acuminata (2025), treated. Otherwise in good health. Most recent cervical screening normal.
PSH: tonsillectomy, age 8.
Medications: ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate, 1 tab daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: breast cancer in her mother at 55; type 2 diabetes in her father.
Social: one male partner; condoms used inconsistently. Nonsmoker.

Exam: External genitalia — a single soft, exophytic lesion adjacent to the perineum, formed of multiple small projections giving it an irregular, cauliflower-like surface. No inguinal lymphadenopathy. Speculum examination: vaginal walls and cervix without additional lesions. Bimanual not indicated.

Assessment: recurrent condyloma acuminatum, perineal.

Procedure: cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen to the lesion, two freeze-thaw cycles, after verbal consent. Tolerated well.

Counseling: recurrence after clearance is common; consistent condom use reduces but does not eliminate transmission. Aftercare reviewed.

Plan: recheck in 4 weeks; retreat if residual.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN PRACTICE — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 03/16/2026

Four weeks after cryotherapy. Patient reports the area blistered and then healed; she has seen nothing new.
Exam: treated perineal site fully healed; no residual or new condylomata on external inspection. No inguinal nodes.

Assessment: recurrent condyloma acuminatum, resolved after single cryotherapy treatment.
Plan: no further treatment needed. Return or contact PCP for any new lesions. Cervical screening per her primary care schedule.

Obstetrics & Gynecology
